executiveSummary.headline: High-Risk Curriculum Modification: Removing "Graph Algorithms (Representations, BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, MST)" triggers cascade across 5 subsequent courses.
executiveSummary.overallAssessment: The proposed deletion of "Graph Algorithms (Representations, BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, MST)" from CSE 207 carries an overall modeled impact score of 76/100 (HIGH RISK). While it relieves 3.5 weeks of course density, it destabilizes prerequisite readiness for CSE 301 (Algorithms) and CSE 401 (Artificial Intelligence).
keyRisks: CLO Coverage Reduction: CSE207-CLO3 drops by 23% (85% ➔ 62%).
Prerequisite Invalidation: 6 downstream topics lose required conceptual foundations.
Downstream Cascade: Direct child course CSE 301 (Algorithms) suffers critical instructional disruption.
Critical Knowledge Gap: Standard OBE competencies in graph representations and search spaces omitted.
executiveSummary.recommendedAction: Adopt Plan C (Relocate topic to CSE 301 Algorithms) or Plan B (Retain 1.5-week core subset) to maintain accreditation integrity.

alternatives.name: Plan A: Proposed Full Removal
alternatives.description: Permanently delete "Graph Algorithms (Representations, BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, MST)" from CSE 207.
pros: Frees up 3.5 weeks in CSE 207 for existing topics.
Reduces initial student cognitive overload in early semester.
cons: Creates severe downstream knowledge gaps in Algorithms and AI.
Breaks CLO-3 accreditation alignment.
Faculty in downstream courses will need to teach prerequisite concepts from scratch.
alternatives.recommendationRationale: Not recommended as-is due to high cascade risk across 3 subsequent semesters.

alternatives.name: Plan B: Scope Reduction (Essential Subset)
alternatives.description: Retain core concepts of "Graph Algorithms (Representations, BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, MST)" (BFS/DFS, Representations) but reduce instructional time from 3.5 weeks to 1.5 weeks. Omit advanced topics like Minimum Spanning Trees and Bellman-Ford.
alternatives.prerequisiteRisk: Medium (Basic traversal preserved; advanced topics deferred)
alternatives.downstreamRisk: Medium (Algorithms can build on basic BFS/DFS)
pros: Frees 2.0 weeks of instructional time in CSE 207.
Preserves prerequisite readiness for CSE 301 Algorithms.
Students maintain exposure to fundamental graph search algorithms.
cons: Leaves less time for hands-on programming projects on graphs.
Slightly compresses coverage of Dijkstra's algorithm.
alternatives.recommendationRationale: Provides a balanced compromise: reduces syllabus congestion while preserving necessary prerequisite readiness.

alternatives.name: Plan C: Curricular Relocation (Move to Algorithms)
alternatives.description: Move the in-depth treatment of "Graph Algorithms (Representations, BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, MST)" to CSE 301 (Algorithms), while keeping only a 1-week conceptual overview in CSE 207. Formally update the CSE 301 course syllabus and credits accordingly.
alternatives.prerequisiteRisk: Low (Taught at the immediate point of need in Algorithms)
alternatives.downstreamRisk: Low (Algorithms syllabus absorbs and structures the topic)
alternatives.curriculumGap: Low (Zero net loss in curriculum-wide knowledge)
pros: Zero total knowledge loss across the degree program.
Allows Graph Algorithms to be taught with greater mathematical maturity in Semester 4.
Eliminates conceptual redundancy between Data Structures and Algorithms.
cons: Requires coordinated syllabus approval across two faculty instructors.
CSE 301 syllabus will need 2 additional weeks of instructional time.
alternatives.recommendationRationale: Model indicates lowest structural risk (26/100). Foundational concepts remain in the degree program without breaking downstream courses.

executiveSummary.headline: High-Risk Curriculum Modification: Removing "Graph Algorithms (Representations, BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, MST)" triggers cascade across 5 subsequent courses.
executiveSummary.overallAssessment: The proposed deletion of "Graph Algorithms (Representations, BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, MST)" from CSE 207 carries an overall modeled impact score of 76/100 (HIGH RISK). While it relieves 3.5 weeks of course density, it destabilizes prerequisite readiness for CSE 301 (Algorithms) and CSE 401 (Artificial Intelligence).
keyRisks: CLO Coverage Reduction: CSE207-CLO3 drops by 23% (85% ➔ 62%).
Prerequisite Invalidation: 6 downstream topics lose required conceptual foundations.
Downstream Cascade: Direct child course CSE 301 (Algorithms) suffers critical instructional disruption.
Critical Knowledge Gap: Standard OBE competencies in graph representations and search spaces omitted.
executiveSummary.recommendedAction: Adopt Plan C (Relocate topic to CSE 301 Algorithms) or Plan B (Retain 1.5-week core subset) to maintain accreditation integrity.

alternatives.name: Plan A: Proposed Full Removal
alternatives.description: Permanently delete "Graph Algorithms (Representations, BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, MST)" from CSE 207.
pros: Frees up 3.5 weeks in CSE 207 for existing topics.
Reduces initial student cognitive overload in early semester.
cons: Creates severe downstream knowledge gaps in Algorithms and AI.
Breaks CLO-3 accreditation alignment.
Faculty in downstream courses will need to teach prerequisite concepts from scratch.
alternatives.recommendationRationale: Not recommended as-is due to high cascade risk across 3 subsequent semesters.

alternatives.name: Plan B: Scope Reduction (Essential Subset)
alternatives.description: Retain core concepts of "Graph Algorithms (Representations, BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, MST)" (BFS/DFS, Representations) but reduce instructional time from 3.5 weeks to 1.5 weeks. Omit advanced topics like Minimum Spanning Trees and Bellman-Ford.
alternatives.prerequisiteRisk: Medium (Basic traversal preserved; advanced topics deferred)
alternatives.downstreamRisk: Medium (Algorithms can build on basic BFS/DFS)
pros: Frees 2.0 weeks of instructional time in CSE 207.
Preserves prerequisite readiness for CSE 301 Algorithms.
Students maintain exposure to fundamental graph search algorithms.
cons: Leaves less time for hands-on programming projects on graphs.
Slightly compresses coverage of Dijkstra's algorithm.
alternatives.recommendationRationale: Provides a balanced compromise: reduces syllabus congestion while preserving necessary prerequisite readiness.

alternatives.name: Plan C: Curricular Relocation (Move to Algorithms)
alternatives.description: Move the in-depth treatment of "Graph Algorithms (Representations, BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, MST)" to CSE 301 (Algorithms), while keeping only a 1-week conceptual overview in CSE 207. Formally update the CSE 301 course syllabus and credits accordingly.
alternatives.prerequisiteRisk: Low (Taught at the immediate point of need in Algorithms)
alternatives.downstreamRisk: Low (Algorithms syllabus absorbs and structures the topic)
alternatives.curriculumGap: Low (Zero net loss in curriculum-wide knowledge)
pros: Zero total knowledge loss across the degree program.
Allows Graph Algorithms to be taught with greater mathematical maturity in Semester 4.
Eliminates conceptual redundancy between Data Structures and Algorithms.
cons: Requires coordinated syllabus approval across two faculty instructors.
CSE 301 syllabus will need 2 additional weeks of instructional time.
alternatives.recommendationRationale: Model indicates lowest structural risk (26/100). Foundational concepts remain in the degree program without breaking downstream courses.
